questions.question: Which of the following union ministries launched the Civil Registration System (CRS) mobile application for registration of births and deaths in October 2024?

options.text: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Home Affairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) launched the Civil Registration System (CRS) mobile application for the efficient registration of births and deaths in October 2024.
 
• The CRS aims to streamline the process of maintaining a nationwide database of births and deaths, ensuring accuracy and ease of access.
 
• The mobile application facilitates real-time registration of births and deaths, ensuring prompt data recording.
 
• This initiative aligns with the government’s vision of Digital India, promoting efficient governance through technology-driven solutions.
 
• The Registrar General of India (RGI), under the Ministry of Home Affairs, is tasked with coordinating and unifying the CRS across the country under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare:**

 
 
• This ministry is primarily responsible for agricultural policies, farmer welfare schemes, and rural development.
 
• Key initiatives include the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN), Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), and Soil Health Card Scheme.
 
• It focuses on increasing agricultural productivity and ensuring food security in India.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment:**
 
 
• This ministry works towards the welfare of marginalized and underprivileged communities such as Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs), and persons with disabilities.
 
• Key schemes include the PM-DAKSH Yojana, Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, and Assistance to Disabled Persons for Purchase/Fitting of Aids and Appliances (ADIP).
 
• Its focus is on social equity, inclusion, and empowerment.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Defence:**
 
 
• This ministry is responsible for managing the defense forces of India, including the Army, Navy, and Air Force.
 
• It oversees defense production, procurement, and the strategic security of the country.
 
• Notable initiatives include the Make in India program for defense manufacturing and modernization of armed forces.
 
 
 
• **Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969:**
 
 
• This act mandates the registration of births and deaths in India for creating a legal record.
 
• The Registrar General of India coordinates the implementation of the act across the states.
 
• Data collected under this act is crucial for demographic studies, public health planning, and issuing legal documents.

questions.question: When did the Green Revolution begin in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1966**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution in India began in **1966**, primarily focusing on increasing agricultural productivity to address food shortages and achieve self-sufficiency in food grain production.
 
• It introduced **high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds** for wheat and rice, along with improved irrigation methods, fertilizers, and pesticides to enhance crop yields.
 
• The initiative was launched during the Third Five-Year Plan (1961–1966), with the formal adoption of HYV seeds starting in **1966**.
 
• Dr. Norman Borlaug, known as the "Father of the Green Revolution," was instrumental globally, while Dr. M.S. Swaminathan led its implementation in India.
 
• The Green Revolution initially benefited regions like Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh due to their favorable irrigation infrastructure and climatic conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Main Theme:**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to the period of agricultural transformation aimed at increasing food grain production through the introduction of HYV seeds, chemical fertilizers, irrigation facilities, and modern farming techniques.
 
• While it brought significant benefits, such as self-sufficiency in food production and poverty reduction, it also led to challenges like environmental degradation, regional disparities, and increased reliance on chemical inputs.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, which of the following states has the highest literacy rate in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kerala has the highest literacy rate in India, as per Census 2011, with an impressive literacy rate of 93.9%. 
 
• The state has consistently maintained the top position in literacy rates since the inception of literacy surveys in India.
 
• This achievement is attributed to Kerala’s strong emphasis on education, supported by a robust public education system and governmental initiatives. 
 
• Programs like **Akshara Kerala** and various literacy campaigns have significantly contributed to improving literacy rates in the state. 
 
• Kerala also boasts one of the highest female literacy rates in the country, which contributes to its overall socio-economic development and gender equality.

• As per Census 2011, Tamil Nadu has a literacy rate of 80.33%, which is above the national average of 74.04%.
 
• The state has made significant strides in education with initiatives like the **Samacheer Kalvi** (Uniform System of School Education) and free lunch programs in schools.
 
• Despite these advancements, it still lags behind Kerala in terms of overall literacy rate.
 
 
 
• **Manipur:**
 
 
• Manipur reported a literacy rate of 76.8% according to Census 2011.
 
• The state has made efforts to improve education through programs targeting rural and tribal populations, but challenges such as lack of infrastructure and accessibility persist.
 
• It shows potential for growth in literacy with better implementation of policies and resources.
 
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh:**
 
 
• Himachal Pradesh has a literacy rate of 83.8%, which is among the highest in India.
 
• The state has achieved this through sustained efforts in providing free education and improving school infrastructure, particularly in rural and remote areas.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of a Chief Minister of an Indian state?

options.text: Is the sole link between Council of Ministers and Governor
Coordinates the functioning of inter-state public service commissions
Guides the framing of the policies for the State

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chief Minister of an Indian state acts as the **chief link between the Governor and the Council of Ministers**.
 
• The Chief Minister **advises the Governor** on various issues, including legislative and administrative matters, as per Article 163 of the Constitution of India.
 
• He/she plays a vital role in **guiding and framing state policies** and ensuring their effective implementation.
 
• The function of coordinating inter-state public service commissions is **not a responsibility of the Chief Minister**. This responsibility lies with the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) or other constitutional bodies as per Articles 315-323 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Chief Minister’s duties focus on state governance, policy implementation, and advising the Governor, making him/her the key executive authority in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Link between Governor and Council of Ministers:**

 
 
• The Chief Minister acts as a bridge between the Governor and the Council of Ministers. He/she communicates decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor and ensures the implementation of the Governor’s decisions.
 
• This role ensures smooth functioning of the state government and adherence to constitutional provisions.
 
 
 
• **Advising the Governor:**
 
 
• The Chief Minister advises the Governor on various issues such as the appointment of ministers, dissolution of the Legislative Assembly, and other administrative decisions.
 
• Article 163 of the Indian Constitution provides that the Governor shall act on the advice of the Council of Ministers, headed by the Chief Minister, except in certain discretionary situations.
 
 
 
• **Inter-State Public Service Commissions:**
 
 
• These commissions are formed under Articles 315-323 of the Indian Constitution to handle recruitment and related matters for two or more states.
 
• The responsibility for their functioning lies with the respective commissions and higher constitutional authorities, not the Chief Minister of a state.

questions.question: Which national festival of India falls on the 26th of January?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Republic Day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• Republic Day is celebrated every year on **26th January** in India to commemorate the day when the **Constitution of India** came into effect in 1950.
 
• The Indian Constitution replaced the **Government of India Act (1935)** and established India as a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic.**
 
• The date, 26th January, was chosen to honor the declaration of **Purna Swaraj (complete independence)** by the Indian National Congress in 1930.
 
• The Republic Day celebrations are marked by a grand **parade at Rajpath, New Delhi,** showcasing India’s cultural diversity, military prowess, and advancements in various fields.
 
• Each year, a chief guest, usually a foreign dignitary, is invited to attend the celebrations, symbolizing India’s diplomatic relations.

• It is the **longest written constitution** in the world, with 448 articles, 12 schedules, and numerous amendments.
 
• It establishes a **parliamentary system of government** with a clear separation of powers among the executive, legislature, and judiciary.
 
• The Constitution guarantees fundamental rights to every citizen, including the right to equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, and cultural and educational rights.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance of Republic Day:**
 
 
• On 26th January 1930, the Indian National Congress declared **Purna Swaraj** (complete independence) as the ultimate goal of India’s freedom struggle.
 
• The date was later selected to honor this historic resolution and mark the transition from colonial rule to a sovereign republic.
 
 
 
• **Other National Festivals of India:**
 
 
• **Independence Day (15th August):** Celebrates India’s independence from British rule in 1947.
 
• **Gandhi Jayanti (2nd October):** Marks the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the leader of India’s freedom struggle.

questions.question: Which title did the Maukharis adopt to imitate the earlier Guptas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharajadhiraja**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Maukharis, a significant dynasty in northern India during the post-Gupta period, adopted the title **Maharajadhiraja**, meaning "Great King of Kings".
 
• This title was originally popularized by the Gupta rulers to symbolize supreme sovereignty and imperial authority over large territories.
 
• By adopting this title, the Maukharis aimed to emulate the grandeur and legitimacy of the earlier Gupta Empire.
 
• The Maukharis ruled regions like Kanauj, Uttar Pradesh, and parts of Bihar in the 6th century CE, seeking to establish dominance amidst competing dynasties such as the Later Guptas and Pushyabhutis.
 
• Historical inscriptions from their reign highlight their use of the title **Maharajadhiraja** as a key indicator of their imperial aspirations and political identity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maharaja:**

 
 
• The title Maharaja, meaning "Great King," was used by regional rulers in ancient India to denote authority over a specific territory.
 
• It was a hierarchical title below Maharajadhiraja, indicating significant but localized power rather than imperial sovereignty.
 
• The Maukharis, aiming for greater legitimacy and supremacy, did not limit themselves to this title and opted for the higher title of Maharajadhiraja.
 
 
 
• **Rajadhiraja:**
 
 
• The title Rajadhiraja, meaning "King of Kings," was another royal designation used to emphasize authority over other subordinate rulers.
 
• It was often adopted by rulers who sought to project dominance but had not yet achieved the imperial stature implied by Maharajadhiraja.
 
• While this title held prestige, it did not convey the same level of sovereignty as Maharajadhiraja, which symbolized supreme imperial power.
 
 
 
• **Samanta:**
 
 
• Samanta was a title used for feudal lords or vassals during ancient and medieval Indian history.
 
• These individuals owed allegiance to higher sovereigns and were responsible for managing their territories and offering military support.
 
• The title lacked the imperial connotation of Maharajadhiraja and was more indicative of subordinate status within a political hierarchy.

__
 
• **Kathak** is one of the classical dance forms of India and originates from **North India**.
 
• It is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures, often accompanied by storytelling through dance.
 
• The word "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word "Katha," which means "story," and the dance form was traditionally performed by storytellers known as "Kathakars."
 
• Kathak evolved during the Mughal period, incorporating elements of Persian and Central Asian dance styles, along with Hindu devotional themes.
 
• It is associated with the states of Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Delhi and is widely practiced in both temples and courts.

• Kathakali performances often depict stories from epics like the Ramayana and Mahabharata, with an emphasis on expressions (Navarasa).
 
 
 
• **Mohiniyattam**
 
 
• Mohiniyattam is another classical dance form from Kerala in **South India**.
 
• It is known for its graceful and feminine movements, often referred to as the "dance of the enchantress."
 
• Mohiniyattam performances are deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and are performed to Carnatic music.

• Kuchipudi performances are typically based on Hindu religious themes and stories from the Bhagavatam and other scriptures.

questions.question: The sale of government assets is also known as:
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Disinvestment** refers to the sale or liquidation of government-owned assets, usually in public sector undertakings (PSUs), to private entities.
 
• The primary objective of disinvestment is to reduce the financial burden on the government and improve operational efficiency by introducing private sector management.
 
• Disinvestment helps raise capital to fund developmental projects and bridge fiscal deficits.
 
• It can be carried out through public offerings, strategic sales, or share sales to private investors.
 
• Notable examples of disinvestment in India include the strategic sale of Air India to the Tata Group and partial stake sales in Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Life Insurance Corporation (LIC).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Commercialisation:**

 
 
• Commercialisation refers to the process of introducing a product, service, or activity into the market for profit-making purposes.
 
• In the context of government-owned assets, it involves making public enterprises more market-oriented without transferring ownership.
 
• It focuses on improving operational efficiency and financial performance while retaining government control.
 
• Unlike disinvestment, commercialisation does not involve the sale of assets but rather emphasizes generating revenue through better management.
 
 
 
• **Capitalisation:**
 
 
• Capitalisation refers to the process of raising funds by issuing shares or debt instruments to finance business operations or growth.
 
• In the case of government entities, it often involves infusing capital into public enterprises to improve their financial health and operational efficiency.
 
• Unlike disinvestment, capitalisation aims to strengthen the enterprise rather than selling its assets.
 
• It is commonly used to address financial challenges faced by PSUs or to fund infrastructure projects.
 
 
 
• **Investment:**
 
 
• Investment refers to the allocation of funds in assets, projects, or enterprises to generate returns or achieve strategic objectives.
 
• In the government context, it involves funding infrastructure, social programs, or public enterprises to boost economic growth.
 
• It is the opposite of disinvestment, as it focuses on creating assets rather than liquidating them.
 
• Examples include government investments in railways, highways, and education sectors.

questions.question: The greatest number, which divides 1938 and 2337 to leave 0 and 3 respectively as remainders, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required number is the HCF of (1938 − 0) and (2337 − 3), which means we need the HCF of 1938 and 2334.

Instead of prime factorization, check the divisibility of both numbers using the given options.

Both 1938 and 2334 are even numbers, and the sum of their digits (21 and 12) are both divisible by 3.

Thus, both numbers are divisible by 2 × 3 = 6.

Other options (11, 13, 14) do not completely divide 1938.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number = 1938 with remainder 0

Second number = 2337 with remainder 3

**Formula Used:**

Required greatest number = HCF of (N₁ − R₁) and (N₂ − R₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ First exact divisible number = 1938 − 0 = 1938

⇒ Second exact divisible number = 2337 − 3 = 2334

⇒ We need to find the HCF of 1938 and 2334.

⇒ Prime factorization of 1938 = 2 × 3 × 17 × 19

⇒ Prime factorization of 2334 = 2 × 3 × 389

⇒ The common factors are 2 and 3.

⇒ HCF = 2 × 3 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Remainders Case

To find the greatest number dividing x, y and z leaving remainders a, b and c respectively, calculate the HCF of (x−a), (y−b) and (z−c).

LCM with Same Remainder Case

To find the smallest number which when divided by x, y and z leaves remainder r in each case, calculate LCM(x, y, z) + r.

Product of Two Numbers

For any two natural numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF(A, B) × LCM(A, B).
</p

questions.question: The largest four-digit number which when divided by 9, 18 and 23, leaves a remainder 5 in each case, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required number must be of the form: LCM(9, 18, 23) × k + 5.

The LCM of 9, 18, and 23 is 414.

The largest 4-digit number is 9999. Dividing 9999 by 414 gives a quotient of 24 and a remainder of 63.

Largest 4-digit multiple of 414 = 9999 − 63 = 9936.

Required number = 9936 + 5 = 9941.

**∴ The correct answer is 9941.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors: 9, 18, and 23

Remainder in each case = 5

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = [Largest 4-digit multiple of LCM of the divisors] + Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, find the prime factorization to calculate the LCM of 9, 18, and 23.

⇒ 9 = 3²

⇒ 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ 23 = 23 (Prime number)

⇒ LCM = 2 × 3² × 23 = 18 × 23 = 414

⇒ The largest 4-digit number is 9999.

⇒ Divide 9999 by the LCM (414) to find the largest multiple within the 4-digit range.

⇒ 9999 ÷ 414 = 24 with a remainder of 63.

⇒ The largest 4-digit multiple of 414 = 9999 − 63 = 9936.

⇒ This implies that 9936 is completely divisible by 9, 18, and 23.

⇒ Since we need a remainder of 5 in each case, we add 5 to this multiple.

⇒ Required number = 9936 + 5 = 9941.

**∴ The correct answer is 9941.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

When a number divided by a, b, and c leaves remainders x, y, and z respectively, and the differences (a−x) = (b−y) = (c−z) = d are equal, the number is in the form LCM(a, b, c) × k − d.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a person covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Given speeds are x = 78 km/hr and y = 91 km/hr.

Average Speed = (2 × 78 × 91) ÷ (78 + 91)

Average Speed = (2 × 78 × 91) ÷ 169

Average Speed = 2 × 6 × 7 = 84 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 84 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Pune to Mumbai = 78 km/hr

Speed from Mumbai to Pune = 91 km/hr

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 Pune

 Speed = 91 km/hr
 
•

**Formula Used:**

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the one-way distance be the LCM of the speeds (78 and 91) to simplify calculations.

⇒ 78 = 13 × 6 and 91 = 13 × 7

⇒ LCM of 78 and 91 = 13 × 6 × 7 = 546

⇒ Let the distance between Pune and Mumbai be 546 km.

⇒ Time taken from Pune to Mumbai = Distance ÷ Speed = 546 ÷ 78 = 7 hours.

⇒ Time taken from Mumbai to Pune = Distance ÷ Speed = 546 ÷ 91 = 6 hours.

⇒ Total Distance covered = 546 + 546 = 1092 km.

⇒ Total Time taken = 7 + 6 = 13 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = 1092 ÷ 13 = 84 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 84 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Different Distances

When travelling different distances D₁, D₂ at speeds S₁, S₂ respectively, Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time) = (D₁ + D₂) ÷ (D₁/S₁ + D₂/S₂).

Average Speed for 3 Equal Distances

When a person travels 3 equal distances at speeds x, y, and z, the Average Speed = 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). When moving in the same direction, it is the difference (S₁ − S₂).

questions.question: What is the effective discount per cent if a shopkeeper offers a scheme, “Buy five and get three free”?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective Discount % = (Free Items ÷ Total Items) × 100

Here, Free Items = 3

Total Items = 5 (Paid) + 3 (Free) = 8

Discount % = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Buy 5 (Paid)
 
 
 
 
 
 Get 3 (Free)
 
 Total Items = 5 + 3 = 8
 

 Discount % = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%

**Given:**

Scheme = Buy 5, get 3 free.

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Total Discount ÷ Total Marked Price) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the marked price of 1 item be ₹10.

⇒ Total items taken by the customer = 5 (paid) + 3 (free) = 8 items.

⇒ Total marked price of 8 items = 8 × 10 = ₹80.

⇒ Total selling price (since customer pays for only 5 items) = 5 × 10 = ₹50.

⇒ Total Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price = 80 − 50 = ₹30.

⇒ Effective Discount % = (30 ÷ 80) × 100

⇒ Effective Discount % = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

When two discounts of a% and b% are given successively on an article, the net effective discount % is given by the formula: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price and Cost Price Relation

The direct relationship between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP) when dealing with a profit P% and discount D% is: MP × (100 − D)% = CP × (100 + P)%.

Combined Free Scheme and Additional Discount

If a shopkeeper offers a "Buy X Get Y Free" scheme along with an additional z% discount, the overall Selling Price is given by: SP = MP × [X ÷ (X + Y)] × [(100 − z) ÷ 100].

questions.question: Manish travels from City A to City B. If Manish drives his car at 1/3​ of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 36 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Manish would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio (Normal : New) = 3 : 1

Time ratio (Normal : New) = 1 : 3 (Since time is inversely proportional to speed)

Difference in time ratio = 3 − 1 = 2 units

2 units → 36 minutes late

1 unit (Normal time) → 18 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 18 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Time = T min
 
 
 New: Speed = S / 3
 Time = (T + 36) min

**Given:**

New speed = 1/3 of normal speed

Time delay = 36 minutes late

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

When distance is constant, Speed × Time = Constant

**Calculation:**

Let the normal speed be S and normal time be T.

⇒ Normal distance = S × T

⇒ New speed = S / 3

⇒ New time = T + 36

Since the distance traveled is the same in both cases:

⇒ S × T = (S / 3) × (T + 36)

⇒ T = (T + 36) / 3

⇒ 3T = T + 36

⇒ 2T = 36

⇒ T = 18 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 18 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality of Speed and Time

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time. If speed is reduced to a/b of its original value, the time taken becomes b/a of the original time.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy / (x + y).
